slides.title: std::map Overview
slides.prompt: std::map stores key-value pairs sorted automatically by key using self-balancing binary search trees (Red-Black Trees). Search, insert, and delete take O(log N) logarithmic time.

slides.title: operator[] vs at()
slides.prompt: What happens when accessing a non-existent key using map[key] vs map.at(key)?
options: operator[] inserts a default-constructed value; at() throws std::out_of_range
operator[] throws exception; at() inserts default value
slides.correctAnswer: operator[] inserts a default-constructed value; at() throws std::out_of_range

slides.title: Value Type in Map Iteration
slides.prompt: When iterating over std::map, elements are represented as std::pair<const Key, ___>.
slides.codeSnippet:

slides.title: std::multimap Key Duplication
slides.prompt: How does std::multimap differ from std::map?
options: std::multimap allows multiple elements to share the exact same key
std::multimap uses hash tables instead of trees
std::multimap does not keep keys in sorted order
std::multimap supports operator[] with multiple indexes
slides.correctAnswer: std::multimap allows multiple elements to share the exact same key
